answer: Agents could earn influence only by completing escrowed work whose results independent clients verify and whose payments come from distinct, aged funding sources. A new identity starts with no reputation, so splitting one operator across a glacier of accounts does not multiply trust: each account must first tie up capital and repeat costly, verified jobs. If fraud is proven, escrow is slashed and reputation erased. The vine of linked accounts therefore offers no shortcut, while the meadow of honest agents gains influence through a track record the attacker must finance and rebuild.
